subject: Forensic snapshot request — access/logs check
messages:
From: Sara Mitchell <sara.mitchell@pegasusbank.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: secops@pegasusbank.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Request: snapshot of access logs and assertion of no-record-export

Avery —

Following the incident window we discussed yesterday (2026-11-02 22:40–23:05 UTC), our security team is requesting an independent snapshot of any read/export activity that touched Pegasus customer records. Specifically we need:

- A list of any successful read/download/stream requests referencing customer identifiers (partial ok) during the window
- Hashes of the log files you used in your review so we can reconcile provenance
- Confirmation that there was no bulk export or exfiltration of Pegasus records

We appreciate an initial response and an ETA for the forensic artifacts. If you can provide a signed statement of non-export once you complete the reconciliation, that will help close our internal ticket.

Thanks,
Sara Mitchell
Director, Information Security
Pegasus Bank

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mitchell <sara.mitchell@pegasusbank.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Request: snapshot of access logs and assertion of no-record-export

Sara —

Thanks for the note and the clear ask. We started the forensic pull immediately after the window closed. Quick summary/plan: 

1) We'll deliver a CSV of log file hashes and an S3 manifest snippet so your team can verify coverage.
2) We'll share an evidence summary PDF that walks through our reconciliation steps and results.
3) If our verification shows no export, I'll send an official statement confirming there was no customer-record export for Pegasus during the window.

ETA: initial artifacts (hash CSV + manifest snippet) by EOD today (2026-11-03). Full summary and signed assertion by EOD tomorrow (2026-11-04).

I've looped in Stephanie (for the hash reconciliation) and Jonas (for the audit trail) so they can attach the artifacts and notes.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Senior Solutions Engineer — Security
Redwood Inference
Attachment: none (will follow)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mitchell <sara.mitchell@pegasusbank.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 13:18:00 -05:00
Subject: Forensic artifacts: hash list + manifest (pegasus window)

Sara / team —

Attached are the artifacts from our internal audit run covering 2026-11-02 22:40–23:05 UTC:

Attachments (stubs):
- pegasus_log_hashes_20261103.csv (CSV, 4KB) — SHA256 hashes for each rotated log file considered in the window
- s3_manifest_snippet.txt (TXT, 1KB) — key prefixes and byte ranges we reconciled

Executive notes (short):
- We scanned read and object-access events across the serving fleet (in-memory requests, KV-cache hits, and backend object fetches). No object write/put operations were observed that would indicate a bulk export.
- Total unique read events touching Pegasus identifiers in the window: 3 (all service-initiated health probes and one developer debugging call tied to a support session).
- The developer debugging call was authenticated and limited in scope; no downstream archive/export was created.

Jonas is preparing the chain-of-custody summary and will include the signed PDF. After he finalizes that, Avery will send a formal no-export assertion statement.

If you want additional fields in the CSV (IP, requester-id) for internal reconciliation, say the word and we can provide a redacted variant.

—Stephanie
S. Nguyen
Forensics Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: pegasus_log_hashes_20261103.csv

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mitchell <sara.mitchell@pegasusbank.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -05:00
Subject: Final: forensic snapshot + no-export assertion for Pegasus window

Sara —

Attached: forensic_snapshot_summary_pegasus_20261103.pdf (PDF, 88KB) — contains reconciliation steps, hash reconciliation table, and chain-of-custody log. Key findings below: 

1) Hash reconciliation: all log file SHA256 values provided to Pegasus match the copies retained in our secure archive (see CSV). No tampering detected.
2) Read/export activity: three distinct read events were found; none correspond to export operations (no multipart downloads, no bulk S3 list-and-get patterns).
3) Credential/API activity: all calls in the window were from internal service principals and one support engineer; no API keys from Pegasus production credentials were used.
4) No indicators of data-at-rest movement to external endpoints were identified.

Conclusion (formal): Based on our forensic review of the indicated window and the reconciled artifacts, Redwood Inference affirms that there was no export or exfiltration of Pegasus customer records attributable to operations within our environment during 2026-11-02 22:40–23:05 UTC.

We are prepared to sign a short attestation letter on Redwood letterhead and share any redacted logs you require for your compliance file. Please confirm if the provided artifacts satisfy your QA team or whether you need additional redaction fields (IP, request-id).

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Director, Platform Audit & Integrity
Redwood Inference
Attachments: forensic_snapshot_summary_pegasus_20261103.pdf, pegasus_log_hashes_20261103.csv, s3_manifest_snippet.txt
